req.title: Create schema on startup
req.statement: The system shall create the tasks table via SQLAlchemy metadata at application startup.

doc.reasoning: R-TASK-024 requires that the tasks table is created via SQLAlchemy metadata at application startup. The key observable behaviour is: (1) after importing the app, the tasks table exists in the database and the root endpoint responds with HTTP 200 and the expected payload (positive/EP); (2) the tasks table is inspectable and contains the 'tasks' table name (positive/STC — schema state after startup); (3) a GET /tasks/ call immediately after startup returns HTTP 200 with a list (not a 500 from a missing table) — boundary: zero rows in a fresh in-memory DB (BVA); (4) a POST to /tasks/ with a valid payload succeeds with HTTP 201 proving the table is writable (positive/DT); (5) a POST with a missing required field (title=null) returns HTTP 422 proving schema validation is active (negative/NEG). All tests use an in-memory SQLite engine so they are isolated, deterministic, and idempotent.

from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from app.main import app

def test_startup_root_endpoint_returns_200_and_exact_payload():
    client = TestClient(app)
    r = client.get("/")
    assert r.status_code == 200
    body = r.json()
    assert body["message"] == "Welcome to Task Manager API"
    assert body["docs"] == "/docs"
    assert body["version"] == "1.0.0"

from sqlalchemy import inspect as sa_inspect
from app.database import engine
from app.main import app  # ensure startup side-effects have run

def test_startup_tasks_table_exists_in_engine():
    inspector = sa_inspect(engine)
    table_names = inspector.get_table_names()
    assert "tasks" in table_names
    assert table_names.count("tasks") == 1

test_startup_tasks_table_exists_in_engine()

from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from app.main import app

def test_startup_post_task_succeeds_proving_table_writable():
    client = TestClient(app)
    payload = {"title": "Buy groceries", "description": "A", "completed": True}
    r = client.post("/tasks/", json=payload)
    assert r.status_code == 201
    body = r.json()
    assert isinstance(body["id"], int)
    assert body["title"] == "Buy groceries"
    assert body["description"] == "A"
    assert body["completed"] is True
    assert "created_at" in body

tests.name: test_startup_metadata_create_all_idempotent_second_import
preconditions: Calling create_all again must not raise
expected: 'tasks' still in table names after second create_all call
trace: R-TASK-024: create_all is idempotent; repeated startup must not corrupt schema
tests.executable:
from sqlalchemy import inspect as sa_inspect
from app.database import engine
from app import models
from app.main import app  # first create_all

def test_startup_metadata_create_all_idempotent_second_import():
    # Second explicit call must not raise
    models.Base.metadata.create_all(bind=engine)
    inspector = sa_inspect(engine)
    table_names = inspector.get_table_names()
    assert "tasks" in table_names
    assert table_names.count("tasks") == 1

test_startup_metadata_create_all_idempotent_second_import()
